title: Trump’s New Coercive Toolkit

Trump’s New Coercive Toolkit

Tom Miller

Gavekal Research | 13 Aug 2026

On August 7, the US Senate passed an amended Russian sanctions bill authorizing the president to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the world’s top five purchasers of Russian oil and gas. The bill still has to get through the House of Representatives, which may be reluctant to give Donald Trump further sweeping tariff powers. But if it becomes law, it could set a precedent for secondary tariffs as a standard sanctions instrument.As Trump rebuilds his tariff regime, he is increasingly making access to the US market conditional on behavior that has little to do with bilateral trade. More broadly, he is integrating tariffs, sanctions, industrial policy and export controls to pursue geopolitical ends. This risks reigniting international trade spats—notably with India.
